statement: The crypto module implements only the frozen crypto-v1 suite; algorithm choice is explicitly neither archive-negotiable nor caller-negotiable.
evidence_in_source: module doc comment; no algorithm selection parameters exist in public options
research_needed: Independent security review confirming no downgrade or alternate-suite path is reachable from public bytes.

statement: Public crypto API re-exports: encrypt/open/inspect/verify encrypted archives, add_recipient, change_password, reencrypt_recipients, embed_signature, encrypted random access, signature types and functions (sign_archive, verify_signature, current_bindings, read_detached_signature), and TimestampPolicy/TimestampTrustAnchor.

Crypto required-incompatibility feature bits: 0x20 encrypted-indexed, 0x40 payload-suite, 0x80 X-Wing recipient, 0x100 password recipient, 0x200 Ed25519 signature, 0x400 padding, 0x800 strong (PHTE) boundary, 0x1000 private resource declaration (corrected Descriptor v2).
The supported CRYPTO_FEATURES mask includes the signature bit 0x200, although the wire spec header still says bit 0x200 remains unsupported by the Rust reader mask.
refines_or_supersedes: Contradicts docs/crypto-wire-v1.md §Required incompatibility features L15-17; consistent with docs/crypto-wire-v1.md §SignatureRecordV1 L713-717 and docs/crypto-implementation-v1.md L95-96
decision_needed: Which statement is authoritative for bit 0x200 support, and should the wire document header be corrected?

statement: Feature 0x1000 marks the corrected encrypted Descriptor v2 carrying private resource declarations; unencrypted ECF encoding refuses it with EB_UNSUPPORTED_REQUIRED_FEATURE.
refines_or_supersedes: Implements correction in docs/crypto-implementation-v1.md §Descriptor-v2 schema correction L173-203

statement: Frozen sizes: X-Wing public key 1216 bytes, X-Wing secret seed 32 bytes; local key file header 12 bytes with magic EBK1.
PaddingMode enum: None=0, Bucketed=1 (default), Maximum=2; any other byte is NONCONFORMING with EB_CRYPTO_PADDING_INVALID.
BoundaryMode enum: SecretGearTable=1 (default), PhteAes128=2; any other byte is UNSUPPORTED with EB_CRYPTO_BOUNDARY_MODE_UNSUPPORTED.
ProtectionPolicy has only HybridOnly=1 and PasswordOnly=2 and is crate-private; no mixed, classical-only, or multi-password policy value exists.
refines_or_supersedes: Implements docs/crypto-wire-v1.md L45-46; docs/crypto-suite-v1.md §Classical recipient policy L473-479

statement: Archives cannot combine X-Wing recipients with a password, cannot hold more than one password stanza, and cannot use classical-only recipients; creation with both recipients and a password is refused (EB_CRYPTO_RECIPIENT_POLICY_INVALID).
refines_or_supersedes: Frozen by docs/crypto-suite-v1.md L462-466, L475-485; docs/crypto-implementation-v1.md L12-13, L217-219
research_needed: Usability evidence on recovery workflows (e.g., escrow password plus hybrid recipients) to confirm the no-mix rule is acceptable.
decision_needed: Should a future version define a separate recovery or classical protection class, and is the single-password limit acceptable for v1?

statement: CryptoPolicy is a caller-owned cap set for attacker-controlled crypto work: stanza count, stanza bytes, envelope bytes, identity attempts, Argon2 memory/passes/parallelism, segments, messages per segment, ciphertext record bytes, private record bytes, and working memory.
refines_or_supersedes: Implements docs/crypto-implementation-v1.md §Resource and materialization policy L160-165

statement: Default CryptoPolicy: 1024 stanzas, 65536 stanza bytes, 16 MiB envelope, 4096 identity attempts, 1,048,576 KiB Argon2 memory, 10 passes, parallelism 16, 1,000,000 segments, 2^20-1 messages/segment, 64 MiB+16 ciphertext record, 64 MiB private record, 1 GiB working memory; no measurement justifies them in code.
refines_or_supersedes: Mirrors limits in docs/crypto-wire-v1.md L245-246, L440-443
research_needed: Measure worst-case CPU time, peak memory, and allocation for each limit on adversarial archives on low-memory and desktop reference hosts.
decision_needed: Are the default open-time crypto limits appropriate for untrusted input on constrained devices?

statement: Default caller Argon2 limits equal the frozen wire ceiling (1 GiB, 10 passes, parallelism 16), so by default an untrusted password archive may demand the maximum KDF cost per unlock attempt.
research_needed: Benchmark Argon2id at 1 GiB/10 passes on reference low-end hardware; assess denial-of-service impact of hostile archives.
decision_needed: Should the default open policy be lower than the wire ceiling (for example the 256 MiB/3-pass creation default)?

statement: Up to 4096 (identity, stanza) trial unlocks are permitted by default; the per-attempt cost of X-Wing decapsulation, HKDF, and AEAD wrap-open is not measured.
research_needed: Benchmark unlock latency for 1024 stanzas with several identities; confirm the 4096 budget bounds worst-case time acceptably.

statement: XWingRecipient::from_bytes requires exactly 1216 bytes that parse as an X-Wing encapsulation key (else EB_CRYPTO_RECIPIENT_STANZA_INVALID) and a label of at most 1024 bytes (else EB_CRYPTO_RESOURCE_POLICY_REFUSED); Debug shows only fingerprint and label.
Recipient public-key validation delegates to x-wing 0.1.0 EncapsulationKey::try_from; whether FIPS 203 encapsulation-key (modulus) checks run is not established in Entrybound code or tests.
research_needed: Inspect x-wing/ml-kem crate source and test with non-reduced ML-KEM key coefficients and malformed X25519 components.

statement: Recipient fingerprint is the full 32-byte SHA-256 of T1("entrybound/recipient-public-key/v1", [kind u16=1, public key]); used for duplicate-input detection and the private recipient directory.
evidence_in_source: code; duplicate refusal tested in crypto_v1.rs L173-181

statement: Local EBK1 key file: magic, u16 version 1, u16 kind (1 recipient public key, 2 identity seed), u32 payload length, payload; exact-length strict decoding; recipient file 1228 bytes, identity 44 bytes; recipient labels are not persisted.
refines_or_supersedes: Implements docs/crypto-implementation-v1.md §Keys, recipients, and local key files L78-83

statement: The EBK1 header contains no flags or reserved bytes (magic, version, kind, length only), although the implementation note claims flags and reserved bytes are strictly checked.
decision_needed: Correct the implementation note, or add flags/reserved fields before the EBK1 format is relied upon?

statement: X-Wing identity files store the raw 32-byte seed unencrypted; there is no passphrase-protected key file, OS keychain, agent, KMS, or HSM storage, and file permissions are the caller's responsibility.
research_needed: Threat-model and usability study of plaintext identity files versus protected key storage.
decision_needed: Is unencrypted identity-file storage acceptable for v1, or is passphrase/keychain/hardware-backed storage required?

statement: XWingIdentity Debug prints only REDACTED; generate() uses the x-wing crate keypair generator (getrandom feature), from_seed accepts any 32-byte seed, and recipient() returns an empty-label public recipient.
XWingIdentity has no explicit Zeroize/ZeroizeOnDrop; secret erasure relies on the x-wing crate zeroize feature for DecapsulationKey, including any expanded ML-KEM/X25519 key state.
research_needed: Audit x-wing 0.1.0 drop behaviour and run a memory-residue test after identity drop.

statement: Unlock supports only a borrowed in-memory X-Wing identity or password bytes; no hardware token, KMS, plugin, or agent unlock mechanism exists.
decision_needed: Is plugin/hardware-backed unlock needed for v1 or deferred?

statement: Secret32 zeroizes on drop; KeyHierarchy derives Zeroize and ZeroizeOnDrop over root PRK, commitment, envelope-MAC, control-segment, payload-segment, default-boundary (32 bytes) and strong-boundary poly/PRF (16 bytes) keys.

Root hierarchy: root_salt=SHA-256(T1 root-salt/v1 [namespace, major, minor, crypto 1, suite 1, archive_id]); root_prk=HKDF-Extract(root_salt, AFK); seven children derived with empty context under frozen purpose labels.
refines_or_supersedes: Implements docs/crypto-suite-v1.md §Archive file key and root hierarchy L57-112
evidence_in_source: test mod.rs::frozen_v1_to_v4_construction_vectors checks root PRK and all subkeys

statement: Format major 0 and minor 1 are hard-coded constants in root-salt, commitment, public crypto context, and wrap-AD transcripts, not read from the archive Descriptor; the signature content binding instead uses Descriptor values.
refines_or_supersedes: Spec fields are format_major/format_minor in docs/crypto-suite-v1.md L73-74, L121-122
evidence_in_source: code; V1 vector uses version 0.1 (docs/crypto-wire-v1.md L806)
decision_needed: When the ECF format version changes (e.g. a 1.0 release), do crypto transcripts keep 0.1 constants or follow the Descriptor, and how are existing 0.1 encrypted archives read?

statement: Crypto-v1 is labelled experimental and already carries a legacy compatibility form (pre-bb8cca9 Descriptor v1); the policy for retiring experimental forms and freezing encrypted bytes before v1 release is unresolved in code.
evidence_in_source: implementation note status line; legacy vector test (mod.rs L832-869)
decision_needed: Which experimental encrypted byte forms will v1 readers be obligated to open indefinitely?

statement: Extracted PRK arrays are zeroized, but Hkdf instances built from root_prk and recipient wrap PRKs hold HMAC key state whose erasure on drop is not established.
research_needed: Audit hkdf/hmac 0.13 drop semantics or run a memory-residue test on derivation paths.

statement: Secret Gear table: 256 u64 values, each the first 8 big-endian bytes of HMAC-SHA-256(default-boundary key, T1 gear-table/v1 [u16 index]); chunker prefix gear-norm-secret-table-v1; first four values are frozen by test.

The default secret-Gear-table boundary mode is only defense in depth (analogous keyed-CDC designs are broken per spec); its residual boundary leakage under known/chosen plaintext with bucketed padding is not measured.
evidence_in_source: spec cites external research; no Entrybound measurement
research_needed: Implement boundary/fingerprinting attacks from Truong et al. (CCS 2025) against secret-table mode with and without bucketed padding; quantify leakage.
decision_needed: Should PHTE_AES128 become the default boundary mode for v1?

statement: PHTE key: polynomial sampled by rejection over HMAC(strong-poly key, T1 phte-poly-candidate/v1 [u32 counter]) first 16 bytes with top bit cleared, rejecting only 2^127-1; AES-128 key is the strong PRF key; prefix phte-aes128-norm-v1; ranges vector [34,71,93,153,217,256] frozen.

PHTE correctness is checked only against a self-generated range vector and its throughput cost (spec cites 53-165% slowdown in patched Restic) is unmeasured for Entrybound; exhaustion of the u32 counter maps to CORRUPT EB_CRYPTO_BOUNDARY_MODE_UNSUPPORTED.
research_needed: Benchmark chunk_ranges_encrypted PHTE vs Gear throughput; cross-check ranges with an independent PHTE implementation from the paper.

statement: Derived boundary secrets are copied into EncryptedBoundaryKey (Box Gear table, PHTE polynomial, copied AES key), which derives Clone without Zeroize, so these copies are not erased on drop.
research_needed: Memory-hygiene audit of boundary key lifetimes during planning.
decision_needed: Should EncryptedBoundaryKey implement ZeroizeOnDrop and avoid Clone?

statement: pack_directory_encrypted draws a fresh random AFK and archive ID, derives the boundary key, plans the directory with keyed CDC, and assigns planner IDs fast-enc-v1, balanced-enc-v1, dense-enc-v1, or extreme-enc-v1 before encrypting.
evidence_in_source: test: LAI/AUX equal across two packs, PCI differs, chunker_id prefixes checked

statement: Only pack_directory_encrypted and AFK rotation re-chunk under the AFK-derived boundary key; public encrypt_archive encrypts an already-planned Archive, renaming its planner ID to *-enc-v1 but keeping its (possibly public-Gear) chunk boundaries, with no chunker_id check in the crypto container.
refines_or_supersedes: Conflicts with intent of docs/crypto-suite-v1.md L629-633 (enc planner IDs substitute the encrypted chunker)
evidence_in_source: code reading; tests encrypt plan_directory output (crypto_v1.rs L50-59)
research_needed: Confirm chunker_id of encrypt_archive outputs and whether readers accept public-Gear boundaries in encrypted archives.
decision_needed: Should encrypt_archive refuse or re-plan archives not chunked with the encrypted boundary key?

statement: Every encryption uses fresh OS randomness for AFK, archive ID, stanza IDs, wrap nonces, and salts; no deterministic or reproducible encryption mode exists, so identical inputs yield different encrypted bytes and PCI.
refines_or_supersedes: Consistent with docs/crypto-implementation-v1.md L32-34, L217-219; docs/crypto-suite-v1.md L29-30
evidence_in_source: code; test shows PCI differs (crypto_v1.rs L341-343)
decision_needed: Is reproducible encrypted output (e.g., for reproducible builds) a non-goal for v1?

statement: Deduplication is confined to one AFK/archive domain: keys are random per archive, so there is no convergent encryption or cross-archive dedup.
evidence_in_source: code derives all keys from a fresh random AFK

statement: derive() expands root_prk with HKDF-SHA-256 using info T1("entrybound/derive/v1", [purpose, context]); HKDF failures map to CORRUPT EB_CRYPTO_SUITE_UNSUPPORTED.

Key commitment = HMAC-SHA-256(commitment key, T1 key-commitment/v1 [namespace, 0, 1, crypto, suite, archive_id, layout 1, padding, boundary]); features and protection policy are not in the commitment but are covered by the envelope MAC.
evidence_in_source: V1 commitment vector; tamper test crypto_v1.rs L409-414 yields EB_CRYPTO_KEY_COMMITMENT_FAILED

statement: PublicCryptoContextV1 is T1 public-crypto-context/v1 over namespace, format 0.1, crypto, suite, archive_id, layout 1, role 1, required features u64, padding, boundary; vectors for legacy features 0x04ef and corrected 0x14ef come from docs/descriptor-vectors-v1.txt.
refines_or_supersedes: Implements docs/crypto-wire-v1.md §PublicCryptoContextV1 L205-225; corrected by docs/descriptor-vectors-v1.txt L3, L19-22

statement: Layout and archive role are fixed to 1 (INDEXED, Complete) in the commitment and public context: encrypted STREAM output and non-Complete encrypted roles (partial, incremental) are not implemented.
refines_or_supersedes: Frozen by docs/crypto-wire-v1.md L42-43, L131-133; status docs/crypto-implementation-v1.md L14-15, L217-219
research_needed: Survey need for encrypted pipe/tape/unseekable output and encrypted incremental archives.
decision_needed: Is encrypted STREAM (or encrypted partial/incremental roles) required for v1?

statement: Envelope MAC = HMAC-SHA-256(envelope key, T1 envelope-mac/v1 [public context, T1 envelope-core/v1 [public context, commitment, policy byte, exact stanza sequence]]).
evidence_in_source: tamper test crypto_v1.rs L416-421 yields EB_CRYPTO_ENVELOPE_AUTH_FAILED

statement: Recipient method context = T1 recipient-method-context/v1 [stanza version 1, type, class, stanza_id, recipient_hint, method_parameters, encapsulation].
Wrap key: PRK=HKDF-Extract(salt=archive_id, IKM=method secret); key=HKDF-Expand(PRK, T1 recipient-wrap-key/v1 [suite, type, class, stanza_id, SHA-256(method context)], 32).

Wrap AD is the corrected flat 14-field T1 recipient-wrap-ad/v1 (namespace, format 0.1, crypto, suite, archive_id, stanza version, type, class, ID, hint, parameters, encapsulation, nonce); V5 hybrid and V6 password vectors are read from docs/crypto-wire-v1-vectors.txt.
refines_or_supersedes: Supersedes pre-1c9c925 wrap vectors per docs/crypto-implementation-v1.md L121-124 and docs/crypto-wire-v1-vectors.txt L3 (correction dated 2026-08-30)

statement: The AFK is sealed with AES-256-GCM-SIV under the wrap key, stanza wrap nonce, and wrap AD into 48 bytes; any unwrap failure or wrong length collapses to POLICY_REFUSED EB_CRYPTO_NO_MATCHING_RECIPIENT, making wrong keys and passwords indistinguishable.

open_afk decrypts the candidate AFK into a plain Vec<u8> before copying to Secret32; the heap buffer is freed without zeroization, contrary to the note that candidate unwrapped AFKs are held in zeroizing types.
research_needed: Confirm via memory-residue test; switch to a zeroizing buffer.

statement: Unlock failure paths (Argon2 failure, wrap tag failure, and later commitment/MAC checks) share public wording, but timing differences that could reveal which step failed are unmeasured.
research_needed: Timing analysis of wrong-password, wrong-identity, corrupted-stanza, and commitment-mismatch paths.

statement: AEAD is AES-256-GCM-SIV (aes-gcm-siv 0.12.1) with 12-byte nonces; open/seal failures are CORRUPT EB_CRYPTO_AEAD_AUTH_FAILED; HMAC-SHA-256 uses full 32-byte output.

Primitive conformance relies on one vector each (RFC 8452 empty-plaintext, RFC 5869 case 1, RFC 4231 case 1, RFC 9106 Argon2id); no Wycheproof or multi-vector suites run for AES-GCM-SIV, HKDF, HMAC, or Argon2id.
research_needed: Run Wycheproof AES-GCM-SIV/HMAC suites and full RFC vector sets against the pinned crates.

statement: Password method parameters are exactly 36 bytes: "A2ID", u32 version, u32 memory KiB, u32 passes, u32 parallelism, 16-byte salt; wrong length or magic is EB_CRYPTO_RECIPIENT_STANZA_INVALID.

Readers accept only Argon2 version 19, memory 65,536-1,048,576 KiB, passes 3-10, parallelism 1-16, memory >= 8*parallelism, and memory divisible by 4*parallelism; violations are NONCONFORMING EB_CRYPTO_RECIPIENT_STANZA_INVALID.
Caller Argon2 limits are checked after structural bounds and before any KDF work; exceeding memory, passes, or parallelism policy is POLICY_REFUSED EB_CRYPTO_PASSWORD_KDF_POLICY_REFUSED.
password_secret runs Argon2id v0x13 with 32-byte output over the exact password bytes (no normalization); Argon2 errors map to the same no-matching-recipient result as a wrong password.

Writers always use Argon2id 262,144 KiB, 3 passes, parallelism 4 with random salt, not configurable through EncryptedWriteOptions; argon2 0.6.0 is built without a parallel feature, so real unlock latency and attacker cost per guess are unmeasured.
research_needed: Benchmark unlock latency on low-end, mobile, and desktop hardware and estimate GPU/ASIC guessing cost.
decision_needed: Should creation KDF cost remain frozen or become caller-tunable within the wire bounds?

statement: The library applies no password emptiness or strength check at creation (validate_write_options accepts Some(b"")), while change_password refuses an empty new password.
refines_or_supersedes: Relates to docs/crypto-suite-v1.md L529-531 (offline oracle makes strong passwords essential)
decision_needed: Should the library refuse empty or weak passwords at creation, or leave it to the CLI?

statement: Randomness comes from getrandom (OS CSPRNG); RNG failure is returned as POLICY_REFUSED EB_CRYPTO_RESOURCE_POLICY_REFUSED rather than a panic.
refines_or_supersedes: Implements docs/crypto-suite-v1.md L66 (RNG failure is fatal)

statement: Crypto diagnostics use OutcomeClass CORRUPT for integrity failures, NONCONFORMING for stanza/format faults, POLICY_REFUSED for unlock failure, resource limits, and I/O; the spec taxonomy names the integrity class INTEGRITY_MISMATCH.
decision_needed: Is CORRUPT the stable public name for the spec's INTEGRITY_MISMATCH class, and should the spec be aligned?

statement: Unit tests load normative vectors via include_str from docs/crypto-wire-v1-vectors.txt and docs/descriptor-vectors-v1.txt, so the published vector files are executable conformance inputs.

V1-V4 vectors (root PRK, subkeys, commitment, segment key, DATA/END nonces, record AD digest, recipient-set digest, X-Wing combiner hash) are hard-coded hex in the unit test rather than read from the vector file.
research_needed: Verify hard-coded V1-V4 values equal the published vector document to prevent silent divergence.

statement: The V4 combiner test only SHA3-hashes a constructed string; X-Wing correctness rests on three draft-10 KATs, while the spec release gate additionally requires interoperability with an independent X-Wing implementation, which no test demonstrates.
research_needed: Cross-implementation test (encapsulate with Entrybound, decapsulate with an independent draft-10 implementation, and vice versa).

statement: The X-Wing method identifier permanently pins draft-10; handling when X-Wing is finalized with different bytes (new stanza type, migration, dual support) is not defined in code.
refines_or_supersedes: Relates to docs/crypto-suite-v1.md L468-471; docs/crypto-wire-v1.md L752-754
research_needed: Track CFRG X-Wing status and diff final text against draft-10.
decision_needed: What migration path applies to draft-10 archives once X-Wing is finalized?

statement: Signature constants: version 1, algorithm 1 (Ed25519), binding bits CONTENT=1, PHYSICAL=2, ADDRESSING=4 (mask 0x07), maximum timestamp token 65,536 bytes, signing-key file magic EBSK version 1.
AddressingBinding (payload suite ID, recipient-set digest, commitment, archive ID) is documented as physical/authenticated context, not Entrybound semantic identity.
CurrentBindings fields are crate-private; external callers can obtain binding transcripts only through current_bindings() and cannot construct arbitrary bindings for signing.

SigningKey holds a 32-byte Ed25519 seed (Clone, Zeroize, ZeroizeOnDrop, no Debug/Display); EBSK file is magic, version 1, type 1, length 32, seed (44 bytes); read_file zeroizes its buffer and rejects malformed files as CORRUPT EB_SIGNATURE_INVALID.
Signing keys are stored as a plaintext seed file; no passphrase protection, HSM, agent, key rotation/revocation metadata, or keychain integration exists in the library.
refines_or_supersedes: Consistent with docs/crypto-implementation-v1.md L85-87, L217-219; see docs/signing-key-management-v1.md
research_needed: Threat-model review of plaintext signing seeds for release-signing use cases.
decision_needed: Is plaintext EBSK storage acceptable for v1 signing workflows?

statement: Test local_signing_key_is_versioned_and_round_trips checks only magic and length and never calls read_file; EBSK decoding and malformed-file rejection are untested in this slice.
research_needed: Add round-trip and malformed EBSK tests.

statement: SignatureRecord is canonical record type 26 with tags 1 version, 2 algorithm, 3 mask, 4 public key, 5 content binding, 6 optional physical, 7 optional addressing, 8 signature, 9 optional timestamp; encode_without_timestamp stops at tag 8.

SignatureRecord::decode requires exactly one canonical type-26 version-1 record with no trailing bytes, required tags {1,2,3,4,5,8}, optional {6,7,9}, exact 32/64-byte key and signature, valid shape, and byte-identical re-encoding; otherwise CORRUPT EB_SIGNATURE_INVALID.

Shape validation: version or algorithm other than 1 is UNSUPPORTED EB_SIGNATURE_UNSUPPORTED; mask must include CONTENT and no unknown bits; binding fields must be present exactly when their mask bit is set; binding transcripts and timestamp length (1..65,536) are validated.
A binding mask missing CONTENT or carrying unknown bits is reported as UNSUPPORTED, whereas the wire spec says nonzero reserved bits are nonconforming.
decision_needed: Should unknown binding-mask bits be UNSUPPORTED (forward-compatible) or NONCONFORMING?

statement: Ed25519 signs T1 signature/v1 over version, algorithm, mask, public key, content binding, physical presence byte and value, addressing presence byte and value, in pure mode without prehash or context; V7 transcript hash and signature bytes are frozen by test.

The RFC 3161 token (tag 9) is outside the Ed25519-signed transcript, so a timestamp can be stripped, added, or replaced on a detached signature without invalidating it; stripping yields TimestampStatus Absent.
research_needed: Threat-model review of timestamp stripping and substitution for detached and embedded signatures.
decision_needed: Must caller policy be able to require a valid timestamp?

statement: signer_id is the first 16 bytes of SHA-256(T1 signer-id/v1 [public key]) and is derived, not serialized.

Status model: CryptographicStatus {Valid, Invalid, Unsupported}; BindingStatus {Valid, Stale, NotBound}; TimestampStatus {Valid, Invalid, Unsupported, Absent}; SignatureStatus adds signer_id, mask, and optional timestamp Unix seconds.

BindingStatus has no INVALID variant: when Ed25519 verification fails, present bindings report STALE, but the suite spec requires INVALID for content, physical, and addressing; CLI export counts such signatures as stale as well.
refines_or_supersedes: Contradicts docs/crypto-suite-v1.md L673, L715; CLI effect at crates/entrybound-cli/src/lib.rs:1055-1062
evidence_in_source: code; test cryptographic_validity_is_separate_from_binding_freshness checks only cryptographic status
decision_needed: Add BindingStatus::Invalid, or amend the spec to STALE-on-invalid?

statement: CryptographicStatus::Unsupported is never produced: unknown signature versions/algorithms raise errors, and embedded signatures are decoded with error propagation, so one future-algorithm embedded signature aborts opening the whole encrypted archive.
refines_or_supersedes: Conflicts with docs/crypto-suite-v1.md L698-700 (unsupported must not invalidate)
research_needed: Test an archive embedding a type-26 record with algorithm 2.
decision_needed: Should unknown signature algorithms be reported as per-signature UNSUPPORTED statuses rather than failing open?

statement: current_bindings builds content T1 [LAI, AUX, "identity/v1", "ecf/bootstrap-v1", Descriptor format major, minor], physical T1 [PCR], and optional addressing T1 [suite u16, recipient-set digest, commitment, archive ID]; PCI is never bound.

current_bindings trusts the supplied OpenedArchive (whose fields are public) and does not inspect VerificationReport flags, so a fabricated or unverified OpenedArchive yields bindings that sign or verify as current.
research_needed: API misuse review of signing/verification flows in library consumers.
decision_needed: Should current_bindings require a verified-only type rather than a public-field struct?

statement: Identity profile "identity/v1" and namespace "ecf/bootstrap-v1" are hard-coded in the content binding and required by its validator, so signatures cannot bind archives under a future identity profile or namespace without a new signature version.
decision_needed: How will signatures bind archives that use a future identity profile or format namespace?

statement: sign_archive always binds CONTENT, binds PHYSICAL/ADDRESSING by explicit booleans (no library default), and refuses ADDRESSING without current addressing as POLICY_REFUSED EB_SIGNATURE_STALE_ADDRESSING.
refines_or_supersedes: Spec says CLI creation defaults to all three bindings (docs/crypto-suite-v1.md L660-661)

statement: ADDRESSING binding exists only for authenticated encrypted archives; unencrypted archives can bind CONTENT and PHYSICAL only, and the refusal reuses the STALE_ADDRESSING reason code instead of a dedicated code.
decision_needed: Should requesting ADDRESSING on an unencrypted archive use a distinct reason code?

statement: verify_signature rejects malformed or small-order Ed25519 public keys as errors (CORRUPT EB_SIGNATURE_INVALID) and uses ed25519-dalek verify_strict; a failing signature yields CryptographicStatus Invalid.

Strict-verification claims (non-canonical encodings, small-order points, invalid scalars rejected) are tested with only one weak key and one S=L case and depend on ed25519-dalek 3.0.0 behaviour; non-canonical public-key and R encodings are untested.
research_needed: Run Wycheproof EdDSA vectors and published Ed25519 edge-case suites against verify_signature.

statement: Ed25519 checks use RFC 8032 section 7.1 tests 1-3 plus the V7 vector, but V7 was generated with the same ed25519-dalek library, so it is not independent evidence.
research_needed: Regenerate V7 transcript and signature with an independent Ed25519 implementation.

statement: Timestamp status: no token is Absent; token without policy is Unsupported; verification success is Valid with time; EB_SIGNATURE_TIMESTAMP_UNSUPPORTED errors become Unsupported; all other errors become Invalid and their detail is discarded.
Timestamp verification is performed even when the Ed25519 signature is cryptographically invalid; timestamp validity is reported independently of signature validity.

SignaturePolicy::enforce: any requirement with no signatures is EB_SIGNATURE_ABSENT; any cryptographically invalid signature fails the whole set with EB_SIGNATURE_INVALID; each required binding needs one VALID status else EB_SIGNATURE_STALE_CONTENT/PHYSICAL/ADDRESSING.

SignaturePolicy has no trusted-signer input (allowed keys or signer IDs), no timestamp requirement, and no threshold; requirements are satisfied by a valid signature from any key, leaving authenticity entirely to the caller.
research_needed: Usability study of CLI users interpreting signer IDs; misuse analysis of --require-signature without key pinning.
decision_needed: Should library and CLI support trusted-signer allowlists and a require-timestamp policy in v1?

statement: Entrybound defines no PKI for archive signing keys; verification needs only archive, signature, and a caller trust decision.
Only pure Ed25519 signatures exist; no post-quantum or hybrid signature algorithm is available despite hybrid post-quantum encryption.
research_needed: Threat assessment of long-lived archive authenticity against future quantum forgery.
decision_needed: Is a post-quantum or hybrid archive signature needed for v1 or a later version?

statement: read_detached_signature reads a whole .ebsig file as exactly one canonical type-26 record with no wrapper; read errors are POLICY_REFUSED EB_IO.
Binding comparison: stored binding absent is NotBound; cryptographically non-valid signature is Stale; stored equals current is Valid; otherwise (including missing current addressing) Stale.
refines_or_supersedes: Implements docs/crypto-suite-v1.md L670-676 except INVALID case

statement: Binding transcripts are strictly decoded: content has 6 fields (32-byte LAI, 32-byte AUX, exact identity/v1, exact ecf/bootstrap-v1, 2-byte major, 2-byte minor); physical has one 32-byte PCR; addressing has 2-, 32-, 32-, 32-byte fields.

Embedded signatures exist only inside encrypted EBCS kind 7 CONTROL objects; unencrypted archives support only detached .ebsig signatures, although bit 0x200 is reserved for possible future unencrypted writers.
decision_needed: Should unencrypted native archives support embedded signatures in v1?

statement: RFC 3161 support is attach-and-verify only: with_timestamp_token attaches an externally obtained 1..65,536-byte DER token; no TimeStampReq generation or online TSA client exists.
research_needed: Usability test of obtaining a token for the SignatureRecord imprint with common TSA tooling.
decision_needed: Should Entrybound generate TimeStampReq bytes or ship an optional TSA client?

statement: Embedding rejects only byte-identical duplicate SignatureRecords, so the same Ed25519 signature with and without (or with different) timestamp tokens can coexist as separate embedded records.
decision_needed: Should embedded signatures be unique per signed transcript?

statement: The spec's binding-staleness matrix (repack, recompress, rechunk, metadata change, recipient add/remove, password change) is tested only for add-recipient (addressing stale) and rotation LAI/AUX stability; PHYSICAL staleness after keyed rechunk is untested.
research_needed: Build a test matrix covering every operation row of the staleness table.

statement: Timestamp verification is offline only, for a narrow v1 profile: SHA-256 message imprint with Ed25519 CMS and certificate signatures; no network service is consulted.
Recognized OIDs: signedData, id-ct-TSTInfo, SHA-256, Ed25519 (1.3.101.112), content-type and message-digest attributes, timeStamping EKU; certificate chain depth bound is 16.

TimestampTrustAnchor is a caller DER certificate; TimestampPolicy carries anchors and a caller verification time; certificate validity is evaluated at token genTime. The CLI builds the policy from --timestamp-trust files and the system clock.
Token length must be 1..65,536 bytes and at least one trust anchor must be supplied; otherwise EB_SIGNATURE_TIMESTAMP_INVALID.

Token must be CMS SignedData (else UNSUPPORTED) with exactly one parameter-less SHA-256 digest algorithm, eContentType id-ct-TSTInfo, and exactly one SignerInfo (else UNSUPPORTED); malformed DER is INVALID.

TSTInfo must be version 1 with SHA-256 imprint algorithm (else UNSUPPORTED); hashedMessage must equal SHA-256 of the SignatureRecord encoded through tag 8 and genTime must not exceed the caller verification time (else INVALID).

TSTInfo policy OID, serial number, nonce, accuracy, ordering, TSA GeneralName, and extensions are parsed but ignored: no policy allowlist, no TSA-name check, no accuracy or clock-skew handling, no critical-extension rejection.
research_needed: RFC 3161 conformance review of which TSTInfo fields a verifier must constrain.
decision_needed: Which TSTInfo fields must the v1 profile check?

statement: SignerInfo must use SHA-256 digest, Ed25519 signature algorithm, and no unsigned attributes (else UNSUPPORTED); signed attributes are mandatory (else INVALID).

The profile pairs an Ed25519 CMS signer with a SHA-256 digest algorithm and signed attributes; RFC 8419 may mandate SHA-512 for Ed25519 with signed attributes, which would make conforming Ed25519 TSA tokens UNSUPPORTED.
research_needed: Check RFC 8419 section 3 primary text and test tokens from an RFC 8419-conforming Ed25519 TSA implementation.
decision_needed: Should the v1 profile accept SHA-512 as the CMS digest for Ed25519 signers?

statement: Only Ed25519 TSA signers and Ed25519-signed certificate chains are accepted; RSA and ECDSA tokens and chains are UNSUPPORTED, and whether any widely used TSA issues Ed25519 tokens is not evidenced.
evidence_in_source: code; only a self-generated Ed25519 token is tested
research_needed: Survey public and commercial TSAs for Ed25519 support; test real tokens end to end.
decision_needed: Should v1 accept RSA-PSS/ECDSA TSA tokens so that timestamps are practically obtainable?

statement: Signed attributes must contain exactly one content-type attribute equal to id-ct-TSTInfo and exactly one message-digest attribute equal to SHA-256 of the TSTInfo DER; duplicates, mismatch, or absence are INVALID; other attributes are ignored.
The ESS signing-certificate (v1/v2) signed attribute binding the TSA certificate is neither required nor checked; certificate-substitution resistance and RFC 3161/RFC 5816 conformance are unverified.
research_needed: Primary-text check of RFC 3161 section 2.4.1 and RFC 5816 requirements; substitution attack analysis.

statement: The signer certificate is found among embedded certificates by issuer/serial or SubjectKeyIdentifier; it needs a critical EKU consisting solely of timeStamping, digitalSignature if KeyUsage is present, validity covering genTime, and an Ed25519 verify_strict signature over DER signed attributes.

Chain building walks at most 16 certificates, succeeds when a certificate's DER equals an anchor, picks the first embedded or anchor certificate whose subject equals the issuer name, requires issuers to be CAs with keyCertSign (if KeyUsage present) valid at genTime, and rejects cycles.

Path validation omits CRL/OCSP revocation, path-length and name constraints, certificate policies, unknown critical extension rejection, AKI/SKI matching, and backtracking among same-named issuers; anchors match by exact DER only.
research_needed: Compare with RFC 5280 path validation; evaluate risk from revoked or compromised TSA keys.
decision_needed: Is a non-revocation-checked, genTime-evaluated chain acceptable for archival timestamps?

statement: All certificate validity is evaluated at the TSA-asserted genTime rather than verification time; with no revocation or timestamp renewal, a compromised expired TSA key could issue backdated tokens that still verify.
research_needed: Long-term validation model review (e.g., evidence-record/renewal approaches such as RFC 4998).
decision_needed: Is timestamp renewal or evidence-record chaining needed for long-term archives?

statement: A leaf or self-signed TSA certificate supplied directly as an anchor is accepted without CA checks, and the sole positive test uses exactly that configuration; intermediate chains, EKU failures, future genTime, and non-Ed25519 tokens lack tests.
research_needed: Add tests for intermediate CA chains, missing/non-critical EKU, future genTime, unsupported algorithms, and cycles.

statement: Algorithm identifiers must have absent parameters; SHA-256 AlgorithmIdentifiers encoded with explicit NULL parameters are UNSUPPORTED, although RFC 5754 reportedly requires accepting both forms.
evidence_in_source: code; RFC 5754 requirement needs primary check
research_needed: Verify RFC 5754 section 2 text and inspect real TSA tokens for NULL digest parameters.
decision_needed: Should NULL parameters be accepted for SHA-256 identifiers?

statement: Timestamp diagnostics: invalid is CORRUPT EB_SIGNATURE_TIMESTAMP_INVALID; unsupported is UNSUPPORTED EB_SIGNATURE_TIMESTAMP_UNSUPPORTED; missing anchors and malformed ContentInfo DER are INVALID rather than UNSUPPORTED.
The only timestamp unit test builds a self-signed Ed25519 TSA certificate and token at wall-clock time, verifies success, an imprint mismatch (INVALID), and a malformed anchor (INVALID).
RFC 3161 parsing depends on the pre-release crate cms =0.3.0-pre.2 plus x509-cert 0.3.0 and der 0.8.1; long-term maintenance and stability of this dependency set is unassessed.
research_needed: Dependency audit (maintenance, advisories, API stability) for cms/x509-cert/der.
decision_needed: Is a pre-release cms crate acceptable in a v1 release?

statement: Attacker-supplied DER tokens (up to 64 KiB) and caller anchor lists are parsed with no fuzz target and no cap on the number of anchors or embedded certificates scanned.
evidence_in_source: absence of fuzz directory in repo
research_needed: Fuzz verify_signature with timestamp policy; bound certificate-set and anchor counts.

statement: Wire constants: namespace ecf/bootstrap-v1, crypto version 1, payload suite 1, X-Wing method string xwing-mlkem768-x25519-sha3-256/draft-10, password method parameter length 36.
Crypto canonical record types: 20 CryptoEnvelope, 21 RecipientStanza, 22 RecipientDirectoryEntry, 23 PrivateFragment, 24 SegmentEnd, 25 ArchiveFinal, 26 SignatureRecord, 27 EncryptedIndexEntry.

Private object kinds 1 canonical record, 2 chunk frame, 3 sequence container; EBCS collection kinds 1 manifest, 2 transform plans, 3 dictionaries, 4 chunk groups, 5 reconstruction data, 6 reconstruction regions, 7 signatures, 8 recipient directory, 9 encrypted index.
Wire limits: T1 at most 65,535 fields; private object at most 1 GiB; EBCS at most 1,000,000 items, 1 GiB total, 64 MiB per item.

T1 encoding: u16 label length, non-empty ASCII label, u16 field count, then per field a 1-based u16 tag, u64 length, and bytes; invalid labels or counts are EB_CRYPTO_PRIVATE_OBJECT_INVALID. Lower-case label form is not enforced.
decode_t1 strictly requires the expected label and field count, contiguous increasing tags, and no trailing bytes; it is marked allow(dead_code) although signature binding validators use it.

RecipientStanza decode requires one complete type-21 record with all tags 1-9, stanza version 1, exact 16-byte ID and hint, 12-byte nonce, 48-byte wrapped AFK, all-zero hint, and byte-identical re-encoding; otherwise EB_CRYPTO_RECIPIENT_STANZA_INVALID.
Recipient hints are always 16 zero bytes in v1: readers trial-unlock stanzas within the identity-attempt budget, preserving recipient anonymity at the cost of no hint-based matching.
research_needed: Measure worst-case unlock time for large stanza sets with several identities.

statement: The wire layer does not validate stanza type or protection class; unknown types remain in the MACed sequence and are skipped (test: type 0x7777 gives EB_CRYPTO_NO_MATCHING_RECIPIENT), while spec says unknown protection classes are not skippable; enforcement of that elsewhere is not shown here.
evidence_in_source: integration test for unknown type only
research_needed: Add a test with an unknown protection class and confirm the container refuses it.

statement: Stanza sequence: 1-1024 stanzas, each at most 65,536 bytes, total at most 16 MiB; u64 count then u64 length plus exact bytes; strictly increasing by (SHA-256(T1 recipient-stanza-sort/v1 [exact stanza]), exact bytes), so duplicates are forbidden.
evidence_in_source: reorder/duplicate tests crypto_v1.rs L461-477; recipient-set vector mod.rs L1020-1039

statement: Stanza sequence decoding checks the 16 MiB size before parsing, count 1-1024, each length 1-65,536, then requires byte-identical canonical re-encoding.

CryptoEnvelope is type 20 with required tags 1-9; crypto version or suite other than 1 is UNSUPPORTED EB_CRYPTO_SUITE_UNSUPPORTED; stanza sequence decoded strictly; byte-identical re-encoding required. Protection policy, padding, and boundary values are not validated at this layer.

EBPO private object: 12-byte header of magic EBPO, u16 version 1, u16 kind 1-3, u32 flags 0, then payload; complete object at most 1 GiB; violations are NONCONFORMING EB_CRYPTO_PRIVATE_OBJECT_INVALID.

EBCS container: magic, version 1, kind 1-9 (unknown kind UNSUPPORTED EB_CRYPTO_SUITE_UNSUPPORTED), flags 0, u64 count at most 1,000,000, items of 1 byte-64 MiB each exactly one canonical record, total at most 1 GiB, no trailing bytes, canonical re-encoding.

EBCS per-kind rules: kinds 2, 7, 8 must be nonempty; allowed record types 1:{3,4}, 2:{2}, 3:{11}, 4:{12}, 5:{14,16}, 6:{18,19}, 7:{26}, 8:{22}, 9:{27}; sort keys strictly increasing, forbidding duplicates.

EBCS sort keys prefix record kind; Entry keyed by path components (encoding byte, u64 length, bytes); plans by u64 ID; audit (19) by u8 target kind, digest, length-prefixed UTF-8 transform; signatures by exact bytes; others by field-1 bytes. The arm at L465-467 is unreachable.

The manifest sort key places each component's encoding byte before its length and bytes, whereas LogicalPath ordering compares component length then bytes and ignores encoding; equivalence for archives mixing component encodings is untested.
refines_or_supersedes: Spec requires Entries by canonical LogicalPath (docs/crypto-wire-v1.md L457)
research_needed: Property test comparing EBCS manifest order with EntrySet canonical order over mixed-encoding paths.
decision_needed: Which ordering is authoritative when component encodings differ?

statement: PrivateFragment type 23 carries 32-byte object ID, u64 total length, u32 index, u32 count, u64 offset, and bytes; count must be nonzero, index below count, and bytes non-empty.

decode_private_fragment checks only cardinality; offset and total-length consistency, contiguity, and byte-identical re-encoding are not checked in this layer, so enforcement of gap-free non-overlapping reassembly must exist elsewhere.
research_needed: Confirm container reassembly checks and add adversarial fragment tests (gaps, overlaps, wrong totals).

statement: Encrypted object ID is SHA-256(T1 encrypted-object/v1 [complete object bytes]); record_kind requires exactly one canonical record.

decode_sequence_container copies every item, decodes each record at least twice, and rebuilds the whole container for canonical comparison, so peak memory may approach several times a container of up to 1 GiB; CryptoPolicy working-memory limits are not consulted here.
research_needed: Measure peak RSS and time decoding maximum-size EBCS containers; evaluate streaming validation.

statement: Wire diagnostics: private framing and T1 faults are NONCONFORMING EB_CRYPTO_PRIVATE_OBJECT_INVALID (even for envelope/signature transcripts); stanza faults are NONCONFORMING EB_CRYPTO_RECIPIENT_STANZA_INVALID.

Wire unit tests cover T1 round trip, the empty-manifest EBCS hex, dispatch of all nine EBCS kinds inside EBPO, and duplicate/reorder/truncation rejection for recipient-directory sequences; limits and envelope/stanza decoding have no wire-level unit tests.
research_needed: Add limit-boundary and envelope decode tests.

statement: Canonical decoders for attacker-controlled public envelope/stanza bytes and private EBPO/EBCS/fragment bytes have unit tests only; the repository contains no fuzz harness.
research_needed: Add cargo-fuzz targets with re-encode differential oracles for CryptoEnvelope, stanza sequences, EBPO, EBCS, and SignatureRecord.

statement: Tamper tests: commitment mutation gives EB_CRYPTO_KEY_COMMITMENT_FAILED, envelope MAC mutation EB_CRYPTO_ENVELOPE_AUTH_FAILED, rehashed ciphertext mutation EB_CRYPTO_AEAD_AUTH_FAILED, footer mutation fails, and truncation gives TRUNCATED_FOOTER or INCORRECT_TOTAL_LENGTH.

Adversarial tests: stanza reorder/duplicate give STANZA_INVALID; unknown stanza type and malformed encapsulation give NO_MATCHING_RECIPIENT; segment reorder and locator mutation give SEGMENT_STRUCTURE_INVALID; splice and END mutation give AEAD_AUTH_FAILED; max_segments=1 gives RESOURCE_POLICY_REFUSED; unknown required bit gives SUITE_UNSUPPORTED.

Mutation tests: add_recipient keeps CONTENT and PHYSICAL valid while ADDRESSING becomes stale; reencrypt_recipients removes the old identity and keeps LAI/AUX; change_password invalidates the old password, keeps LAI/AUX, and changes PCI.

Keyed boundaries derive from the AFK: add_recipient keeps AFK and chunking, whereas key removal and password change draw a new AFK and archive ID and re-plan with new boundary keys, which may change PCR and stale PHYSICAL bindings.
evidence_in_source: code; PCR change after rotation not asserted in tests
research_needed: Test PCR/PHYSICAL staleness after rotation on inputs large enough to rechunk.

statement: CLI crypto workflow test: pack --recipient; public inspect --crypto shows locked metadata; verify without identity prints PRIVATE CONTENT UNVERIFIED; verify/unpack with identity; tampered unpack leaves no destination; sign --embed; verify --signatures --require-addressing-signature; key add/list/remove.
Encrypted crypto-v1 archives cannot carry conversion provenance: preparing encrypted parts for an Archive with conversion data is refused as UNSUPPORTED EB_UNSUPPORTED_REQUIRED_FEATURE.
refines_or_supersedes: Consistent with docs/crypto-wire-v1.md L478-480 (no provenance record assigned)
evidence_in_source: diagnostic text says 'does not yet carry conversion provenance'
decision_needed: Should a crypto provenance record and feature be defined so converted archives can be encrypted with receipts?

statement: Detached signatures of encrypted archives (the CLI default without --embed) expose signer key, LAI, AUX, PCR, format version, recipient-set digest, commitment, and archive ID in plaintext; because LAI/AUX stay stable across re-encryption of identical content, such signatures may enable content confirmation and cross-archive linkage.
refines_or_supersedes: Spec accepts exposure in docs/crypto-suite-v1.md L684-686
evidence_in_source: code reading; tests show LAI equal across encryptions (crypto_v1.rs L341-343)
research_needed: Privacy analysis of confirmation-of-file and linkage attacks using LAI/AUX from detached signatures.
decision_needed: Should the CLI warn, default to embedded signatures, or refuse detached signatures for encrypted archives?

statement: CLI sign binds every binding the archive can provide (CONTENT+PHYSICAL for plaintext, plus ADDRESSING after encrypted unlock), refuses --embed on plaintext archives with EB_SIGNATURE_UNSUPPORTED, and writes detached records with exclusive create.
